Rct3pp.SurfaceDetailHelp: Grain gives textures fine detail up close, where they would look blurred, at almost no cost. Challenge_AquaMountain1: The ruins nearby hint at a loose tie to Atlantis, and rumours of an ancient alien people are spreading. Marketing wants to cash in on the mix-up: give one attraction an Atlantis theme and another a Sci-Fi theme.
Challenge_AquaMountain1Comp: Nicely done - that will bring in plenty of customers.
Challenge_AquaMountain2: A space exploration agency needs a coaster that gives several seconds of weightlessness (air time) to test on 'volunteers', and hiring coaster builders is cheaper than building their own. The free publicity from such a famous partnership will draw lots of guests, and there is a large cash bonus too.
Challenge_AquaMountain2Comp: Congratulations, your coaster meets everything the agency asked for.
Challenge_Atlantis1: The Atlantean embassy wants to show off its newly found city, and will pay us to have two or more Atlantean-themed attractions within a month.
Challenge_Atlantis1Comp: The Atlantean Ambassador says you have caught the old splendour of their lost city perfectly, and rewards you.
Challenge_Atlantis2: First contact with aliens has set off an alien craze, and we should make the most of it. Marketing expects that having 10 or more alien-themed attractions within a month will bring more customers through, plus a large cash bonus.
Challenge_Atlantis2Comp: The aliens we just met may see us as a tasty snack, but your Sci-Fi attractions are a huge hit.
Challenge_CaptBC1: The island music festival season opens soon with Hulapallooza, and the organisers will pay us to give two attractions Paradise Island scenery within two months.
Challenge_CaptBC1Comp: Well done. With boy band The Jolly Rogers having dropped out, this will really lift the festival's profile.
Challenge_CaptBC2: After the 'kebab-gate' scandal, a big fast food chain has gone bust, leaving your kebab supplier with a warehouse full of kebabs. Can you help sell %AMOUNT1% kebabs within two months? Do it and you earn a large cash bonus.
Challenge_CaptBC2Comp: Selling that many kebabs is amazing, and shoppers trust them again. Please take this reward.
Challenge_CastawayGetaway1: Marketing has spotted a growing 'back to nature' fashion among well-off guests that is ready to be tapped. They are sure that two Paradise Island-themed attractions will bring plenty of new visitors and fill our coffers.
Challenge_CastawayGetaway1Comp: Nicely done - now watch the gate numbers climb.
Challenge_CastawayGetaway2: As you surely know, defence cuts have hit the air force's research budget hard, so they are looking for a place to try out their new G-suit. Build and test a roller coaster with very high vertical G's and we win a profitable contract and a boost to our own research.
Challenge_CastawayGetaway2Comp: Nicely done, the air force loves your coaster design.
Challenge_DefaultFailureText: Sorry - the challenge was not completed in time.
Challenge_FoutainofYouth1: In two months this area faces a nasty breeding season of biting Yahoogle Flies. With %AMOUNT1% flowers in the park we can keep it free of them, and earn a cash bonus.
Challenge_FoutainofYouth1Comp: Nicely done, the park is free of Yahoogle Flies!
Challenge_GeminiBasin1: A new computer game, Monkey Monkey, is coming out soon and its publisher wants to launch it in our park! Sell %AMOUNT1% Monkey balloons and the publisher will pay us well (Monkey balloons come from the Safari Hat stall).
Challenge_GeminiBasin2: Monkey Monkey has been a huge failure! Sell %AMOUNT1% Monkey toys (from the Safari Toys stall) within 2 months to empty the overflowing warehouses and get a cash reward.
Challenge_GolfCourse1: We would like Major St. John Smythe to come back. He will feel at home if plenty of guests wear safari hats. Sell %AMOUNT1% within 3 months for a cash bonus.
Challenge_InsectWorld1: Prehistoric is the latest fashion - or so says a popular makeover show. Give 4 attractions a prehistoric theme for our new marketing campaign and we will get loads of publicity.
Challenge_LostLandOfTheDinosaurs1: Dinosaur remains have been found near your park! Make the most of the big news by selling %AMOUNT1% dinosaur masks, and marketing expects hundreds of new guests.
Challenge_LostLandOfTheDinosaurs2: Dinosaurs are all the rage! Promote our new supplier's organic dino burgers. Sell %AMOUNT1% within 3 months and they will give us a fine bonus.
Challenge_MineMountain1: It's Elephant Awareness Week, and the Elephant Council wants more attention. Sell 100 elephant balloons and elephant ears within 3 months and we will get a big publicity boost (both come from the Safari Hat and Safari Toys stalls).
Challenge_MonsterLake1: Goth rock stars 'The Brotherhood of Apocalyptic Unpleasantness' play a concert in town in two months. If the park has four attractions in a fitting gothic style by then, we will draw crowds of moody teenagers.
Challenge_MonsterLake1Comp: You did it - the goths may look a bit glum, but they will love what you have built.
Challenge_MonsterLake2: A record pumpkin harvest has left a mountain of pumpkins. Sell %AMOUNT1% pumpkin pies within three months and the Pumpkin Marketing Board will give us a cash prize.
Challenge_MonsterLake2Comp: You sold all those pumpkins? Did you hide them somewhere? Take this reward.
Challenge_MonsterLake3: The President's recent mishap with our giant foam hand has shaken trust in it. If your well-known park sells %AMOUNT1% foam hands within a month, we will pay you a sales bonus.
Challenge_MonsterLake3Comp: You sold enough foam hands, and trust in them is coming back. Please take this reward.
Challenge_OasisofFun1: The Sheik hates things that clash, and will pay well if two attractions are themed like his palace within one year.
Challenge_OasisofFun1Acc: The Sheik will be happy. Try Adventure scenery.
Challenge_OasisofFun1Comp: The Sheik is delighted. Please take this reward.
Challenge_OasisofFun2: It's time again for 'What Coaster' to hand out its yearly 'Themeys'. We expected to win 'Longest Coaster', but word is a rival has beaten us. Have a coaster of the length below within two months and it will give our marketing a huge lift.
Challenge_OasisofFun2Comp: Nicely done, we are bound to win now, and the publicity will be huge. Remind me to thank you when I collect the award.
Challenge_OneWeekRemaining: The challenge running now ends in one week.
Challenge_OstrichFarm1: A retired hunter, now a reformed man, wants to feel the thrill of the chase once more, and will pay us well to make it happen. If you agree, he lets five animals loose in the park. You then have one week to put them to sleep with the dart gun.
Challenge_OstrichFarm2: The hunter is back, and this time he wants to let ten animals loose in the park. You then have a week to put them to sleep with the dart gun.
Challenge_Pyramids1: Hieroglyphics dug up nearby have been read, and they spell out a curse! The superstitious among us think that setting a great many 'sacred' cats free will lift it and keep us prosperous....
Challenge_Pyramids2: Give 10 attractions the ancient Egypt wall set within 2 months for extra cash and publicity.
Challenge_RaidersOfTheLostCoaster1: Build a coaster that goes faster than 80 miles per hour for a huge publicity boost.
Challenge_RockyCoasters1: The Save the Dancing Bears sanctuary has shut. Show you care by selling %AMOUNT1% bear ears (from the Safari Toys stall) for great publicity.
Challenge_RunDownSafariPark1: Neighbours and visitors are complaining about the awful smell of dung. Clean every bit of it up within 30 days and more visitors will come.
Challenge_SaxonFarm1: Get your guests going by selling %AMOUNT1% donuts within 1 month - all that sugar will get everyone talking about the park!
Challenge_ScrubGardens1: The Save the Dancing Bear world rock festival starts in one month. Sell 10 bear ears to match it for the most publicity (from the Safari Toys stall).
Challenge_TreasureIsland1: Boy band The Jolly Rogers have made pirate clothes the look of the season. If five of our rides have a Paradise Island theme within three months to ride this trend, we should get extra investment and more money for research.
Challenge_TreasureIsland1Comp: Pieces of eight, dude - we're riding the pirate wave now!
Challenge_TreasureIsland2: After the Jolly Rogers' headless parrot fiasco, our suppliers are stuck with piles of pirate goods no one wants. Sell %AMOUNT1% cutlasses within two months and they will make it worth our while.
Challenge_TreasureIsland2Comp: Nicely done clearing that stock, even though the pirate craze is long gone.
Challenge_World_of_the_Sea1: The City Council thinks the city is too drab and wants it livened up. They offer us a big marketing boost if %AMOUNT1% flowers brighten the place.
Challenge_World_of_the_Sea1Comp: Nicely done, the council's grant is ours.
Challenge_World_of_the_Sea2: A new firm hoping to get into top-level motor racing on a tight budget has been in touch. They want to test some advanced car parts, and will pay for a roller coaster with a high top speed and strong lateral G's. Pulling this off will also polish our park's image and bring in more visitors.
Challenge_World_of_the_Sea2Comp: Your coaster meets the requirements - nicely done!

ScenarioAquaMountain_Text: Bubbling ideas are what you need to be at your peak here. Get going, and let your crystal-clear vision have the guests pouring out praise...
ScenarioAtlantis_Text: The Lost City has been found! Fabled Atlantis gives up its riches from the deep - put these wonderful relics to good use and build a park old Neptune would be proud of.
ScenarioBroomLake_Text: The CIA has picked you to build a secret, high-tech park on the once top-secret site of Broom Lake. You have shown you can handle spooks, so don't let THESE "spooks" down, or you may find yourself, ahem, "moved to other duties"!
ScenarioCaptainBlackheartsCove_Text: Ahoy, landlubber! Plunder your imagination and make a fortune from the tale of the dreaded pirate James Blackheart. Win, and your treasure chest fills with pieces of eight - lose, and it's the plank for you!
ScenarioCastawayGetaway_Text: Growing this popular park will take every instinct and survival skill you have - as you tie your plans together and run into the waves, mind you don't end up stranded!
ScenarioCliffCanyon_Text: The setting may come straight from old pulp Sci-Fi stories, but the task is very real: build a park your favourite space heroes would cheer! There are only a few small patches of flat land to build on, but the money for your own space race is already there to grow..
ScenarioFountainOfYouth_Text: The magical Fountain of Youth! This calm, hidden world is a golden chance to refresh your finances - IF you can smooth out the wrinkles in your way!
ScenarioFrightNight_Text: Haunted houses and people in costumes won't do: cheap scares no longer frighten the teenagers round here. Give them something to really scream about - coasters scary enough to make a werewolf lose its fur.
ScenarioGeminiBasin_Text: Gemini Basin is ready for take-off - the robot future of theme parks! Grow a great, towering ape park out of high-tech Sci-Fi attractions - but beware: some robots get far too clever..
ScenarioGhostTown_Text: As in a 1950s horror film, you have been called on to raise the dead. Bring this dusty old ghost town back to life. Dream up a park for guests without much money - and let the bones of the old town pay for your wicked schemes!
ScenarioGoKarts_Text: Formula RCT has pulled into town for a pit stop! This crowd won't be easy to take for a ride, but floor it and give it a go anyway. Remember your seat belt!
ScenarioGoldrush_Text: Here's your chance to strike it rich, using this shaky old mine site to show off low coasters. In time your coasters must make up in thrills what they lack in height, or visitors will lose interest in your claim
ScenarioGolfCourse_Text: The golf tycoon has hit a bogey, and you are left with a below-par course nobody wants - a millstone that is losing money fast. Start a new wildlife park from nothing to bring in a different kind of Tiger.
ScenarioInsectWorld_Text: The last owner was crazy about insects - just look at the anthill of a park he built. Troubles swarmed in until the bank swatted him out of business. Now the park is yours, and so are his debts! You'll need to be as busy as a bee to win.
ScenarioIslandHopping_Text: This tropical paradise makes you want to lie on the beach with a book. The easy-going island resort needs a little jolt of excitement, but with this weather and lifestyle you must keep the park relaxed and still make money..
ScenarioJungle_Text: The farmers here have moved away and sold the place to you. This is your toughest test yet - can you plant the seeds of success, raise the finest wildlife park ever and reap what you sow?
ScenarioLaLaLand_Text: You'll need great people skills, because the Tinsel Town crowd always gets what it wants. Right now it wants a theme park playground all its own. Can you please the biggest egos on earth? Manage it and you'll earn a star on the Walk of Fame.
ScenarioLostLandOfTheDinosaurs_Text: Major St. John Smythe found this lost land, home of the famous Mount Cretaceous. It is on the way to extinction - take charge and turn The Lost Land of the Dinosaurs into a success-o-saurus!
ScenarioMineMountain_Text: You bought this old gold mine to make a theme park, but Wild West parks are pretty tame these days. Can you steer the park somewhere far wilder and stake your claim to fame?
ScenarioMonsterLake_Text: Talk of something hiding under the waters of Monster Lake has stirred up interest in this water park. Sink your teeth into the rivals and set a monster of a park loose on the unwary guests!
ScenarioMountainRange_Text: Bringing grandeur to these mountains will be an uphill climb. You have plenty of money, but little land to build on and locals who are hard to impress. To reach the peak of success, your coasters must be as stunning as the mountains they stand on.
ScenarioMovieBacklot_Text: Watch out, boring amusement parks! A film studio has cast you as the superhero - not in a film, but in the tough job of renewing its tired studio park without spoiling its proud history. You are producer, director and star. Can you give the studio the blockbuster it wants?
ScenarioNationalTreasure_Text: In its prime this huge resort was where anyone who mattered went. Now nobody cares. You've rescued other parks in a sorry state. Can you save this damsel in distress and make her the jewel in the nation's crown again?
ScenarioOasisOfFun_Text: Jump in and make a splash with this lush desert oasis park. Can you hose things down and quench your visitors' thirst for fun?
ScenarioOkCorral_Text: The old frontier calls you to a Wild West park that is about to be retired. Be quick on the draw, round up some improvements and put the Wild back into the West!
ScenarioOstrichFarm_Text: This ostrich farm on the savannah has just come up for sale, and it could be a fine nest egg. It's a perfect home for big game, if an unlikely place for a theme park. Pull your head out of the sand and make this venture a success!
ScenarioParadiseIsland_Text: You've come so far. Now for the last and greatest test - make paradise even better! A dose of coaster madness is needed to cram as many guests as you can onto this jewel of a desert island. It won't be easy - but win, and you'll have reached RollerCoaster Tycoon® bliss.
ScenarioPyramids_Text: Think you know what makes a great wildlife park? Sphinx again! Bring back the old glory of the Pyramids and become a Roller Coaster Pharaoh! As ever, keep the families happy - the Mummies most of all!
ScenarioRaidersOfTheLostCoaster_Text: On his last expedition Major St. John Smythe found the Lost Coaster, a fabled structure spoken of in local legends and thought gone for good. It was built by a people of master coaster builders called the 'Wardleys'. Make this eighth wonder of the coaster world the heart of a splendid new park.
ScenarioRockyCoasters_Text: A badly run safari park nearby has been closed - you'll get great publicity by taking in the neglected animals and setting them free once they are healthy. Turn this well-known theme park into an animal refuge, using all your experience with animals.
ScenarioRunDownZoo_Text: This zoo has been shamefully neglected and is on its last legs. It needs a new approach - a better home for the animals and far more fun for the visitors! In short, an expert makeover, RollerCoaster Tycoon style!
ScenarioScrubGardens_Text: Welcome to Scrub Gardens, just the place for your first venture into animal attractions. Take charge of this small but popular park - learn the basics at Scrubs and clean up.
ScenarioTheMoneyPit_Text: This amusement park shows what happens when good coasters go bad. Can you turn a fixer-upper into a money machine? With plenty of care and an eye for detail you have a chance, but spend wisely or you'll be the one taken for a ride.
ScenarioTransylvania_Text: This old vampire's lair has plenty of atmosphere. Yet somehow it seems a little... drained. Can you sink your teeth in and bring it back to a nice healthy glow - or will you be just another sucker?
ScenarioTreasureIsland_Text: Splice the main brace and shiver me timbers! This is the desert island where Cap'n Keelhauler, 'bloodiest buccaneer in the Caribbean', buried his loot... Dig in and make X mark your spot as the most popular theme park on the seven seas!
ScenarioValleyofKings_Text: Egypt, dry land of ancient mysteries, exotic spices... and stomach-churning rides! That's right - you're swapping camels for coasters to tempt rich tourists out of the bazaars and into your park.
ScenarioVanillaHills_Text: The Vanilla Hills are where your rapid - or not so rapid - climb to RollerCoaster Tycoon® status begins. Can you make this plot the talk of the town? Whether you rate as Apprentice, Entrepreneur or Tycoon hangs on it!
ScenarioWaterTemple_Text: Time to cool down. Use your park building skills in this watery wonderland to make a park fit for such a stunning setting - and one that soaks up as much of your guests' cash as it can. Sink or swim!
ScenarioWorldOfTheSea_Text: This busy water park is already a great catch, but your star performers' fishy appetites are eating you out of house and home! Float some new ideas fast to turn the tide of your cash flow...

TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step10_Text:
Here you set how often the animal keeper fills the food troughs. You may need to do it more often if you add animals to the enclosure or yours seem hungry. With only one or two animals, you might save money by feeding less often.

There is also a button that calls an animal keeper (if one is free) to fill the troughs right away.

Next you'll see how to give the animals toys. Click the Rides button to go on.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step12_Text: Then click the "Animal Enrichment Items" button at the bottom left.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step13_Text: Pick any item in the list and drop it into the enclosure for the animals to play with. Give it a try, then close the items window when you want to go on.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step14_Text: You may know the Attractions list from the original RCT3. It can now list animals too. Click the highlighted Park Management button.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step16_Text: Last, click the Animals tab near the top right of the window.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step17_Text:
Here is every animal in the park. The drop-down list switches what is shown, and clicking an animal's name opens its panel.

Close the list window when you want to go on.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step18_Text: Enclosure fences wear down over time. If no mechanic visits often, a fence can break and animals get out. When that happens, a flashing 'DartCam' button shows at the top right of the screen. Click it now to board the DartCam helicopter.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step19_Text:
To catch an escaped animal, shoot tranquilliser darts at it until it falls asleep. A crate then appears around it. Leave the DartCam (with the Leave DartCam button at the bottom right), click the crate to pick it up, and drop it in an enclosure.

While aiming, right click to zoom in and right click again to zoom out. While zoomed in, left click fires a dart.

Now try to catch the escaped animals. The Next/Previous Escaped Animal buttons switch which one you are looking at. Click Continue when you want to end the tutorial.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step1_Text:
This tutorial shows how to keep animals happy and healthy. There is an enclosure ready with animals, shelters and an animal keeper. You may also spot some escaped animals running wild in the park; later on you'll learn to catch them and put them safely back in an enclosure.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step20_Text: Well done, you've finished this tutorial. Click Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step2_Text: Let's start by looking at an animal's details. Click one of the animals in the enclosure.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step3_Text: Next, click the highlighted Animal Details button.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step4_Text:
This window shows your animal's name, plus buttons to move the view to it, ride along in AnimalCam, sell it, set it free in the wild, and move it to another enclosure.

Click the Animal Stats button for the next step.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step5_Text:
This window shows how healthy your animal is. The bar at the top is its health right now. A healthy animal is more fun for guests to watch and may breed. If health falls, guests who see it may get upset, and an animal left in very poor health for a long time may be taken away.

Under the health bar are bars for the things that affect health. Click Continue to learn what they mean.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step6_Text:
The habitat bar shows how much the animal likes its enclosure. If it is low, the enclosure may be too small or too crowded, or the ground may not suit the animal.

The hunger and thirst bars show how much the animal wants food and water.

The social bar shows how the animal feels about the others in its enclosure. Every species likes a certain amount of company. Some are very sociable and only happy with several of their own kind around; others prefer one or two companions, or none. Even sociable animals have a limit, so watch this bar when you buy new animals.

The cleanliness bar shows how dung is affecting the animal's health. If it gets low, think about hiring more animal keepers or training the ones you have so they clean faster.

Click the highlighted Animal Information button for the next step.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step7_Text:
This window shows facts about this animal and its species.

Click the highlighted Animal Adoptions button for the next step.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step8_Text:
Now and then a guest who sees an animal decides to 'adopt' it, paying a small monthly sum towards its keep. This window lists the guests who have adopted this animal. You can change the monthly fee, but some guests may stop paying if you raise it.

Next, feeding. Click one of the animal houses in the enclosure for the next step.
TutorialText_AnimalCare_Step9_Text: Your animals must be well fed. Animal keepers fill the food troughs now and then, but sometimes you'll want to change how often. Click the Feeding Schedule button to do that.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step10_Text:
Viewing galleries come in three sizes. Pick the smallest and place it on the edge of your enclosure.

The enclosure tools are back on, in case you need to make yours bigger first.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step11_Text:
To let guests use the viewing gallery, join it to a path and open it just like a ride. You can also set what guests pay to use it. The path tools and viewing gallery windows are on if you want to try.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step12_Text: Next, click the highlighted Rides button.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step13_Text: To start adding animals, click the highlighted "Purchase Animals" button.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step14_Text:
To add an animal, click a species in the list, then one of its animal types (an adult male, say).

Once you pick a type, a crate follows the mouse pointer. Click inside the enclosure to drop it there, and it opens by itself.

You can drop animals outside an enclosure too, but they will cause trouble in the park and must be caught again. A later tutorial covers catching them.

Click Continue when you want to end the tutorial.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step15_Text:
Well done, you've finished this tutorial. The next one shows how to look after your animals.

Click Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step1_Text:
Welcome to RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Wild! This expansion adds new rides, scenery and features, and a set of new tutorials introduces them. The tutorials from the original RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3, and from Soaked! if you have it, are still available.

This tutorial shows how to build an enclosure and put animals in it. Click the highlighted Rides icon to begin.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step3_Text:
You can pick from three kinds of enclosure fence - wooden, chain and electric - with the icons at the bottom left of the screen.

To make an enclosure, hold the left mouse button down on the ground and drag. Let go of the button and the enclosure is built.

Click Continue once you've made an enclosure.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step4_Text:
Drag a new enclosure over an existing one to make it bigger. To cut parts away, pick the bin option and click (or click and drag) inside the enclosure.

Every animal needs a certain amount of room. In an enclosure that is too small or too crowded, animals fall ill, and they can't breed if it is too small.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step5_Text: Next, place an animal house. It gives your animals shelter and food. Click the Animal Houses button to start choosing one.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step6_Text:
There are six kinds of animal house, and each animal needs a particular kind. Many houses suit more than one species; the house with the rhino icon, for example, can also hold pandas, camels and hippos. Hover the mouse pointer over a house's icon to see every animal it can take.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step7_Text: Now pick and place an animal house. The enclosure tools are back on, in case you need to make yours bigger first.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step8_Text:
The animal house is where you change the feeding schedule. Guests enjoy watching feeding time, but feeding often costs money and wears out the animal keepers.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Enclosures_Step9_Text:
Each animal house you place comes with an animal keeper, who looks after the animals, feeds them and cleans up. Training her makes her work faster and better.

As well as the keeper that comes with each house, you can hire more in the Staff window, as shown in the RCT3 'Placing Rides' tutorial.

Now add viewing galleries so guests can see the animals properly. Click the highlighted Viewing Galleries button at the bottom left of the screen.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step10_Text: The MixMaster Sequencer is back. Click the text box and type any name you like for your show, then click the highlighted MixMaster Bases button.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step11_Text: Fireworks are launched from firework bases. Click the Mortar button.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step12_Text: Click the ground a few times to put down some mortars, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step13_Text: Click the MixMaster Sequencer button to go on.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step14_Text: Click inside the main area of the MixMaster to add a firework to your show.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step16_Text:
Here is a list of fireworks. Double click one, or click it once and press OK, to add it to your show. The bar beside each name shows how long that firework lasts.

Tip: you can also drag fireworks onto the timeline, which keeps the list open.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step17_Text:
Your firework now sits in the MixMaster Sequencer. How far along it is decides when it goes off; click and drag it to move it along the timeline.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step18_Text:
A firework only shows once it is tied to a base. Click the firework in the MixMaster Sequencer, then click a base (a mortar, say) in the main view. Try it now.

Once tied, the base glows white whenever that firework is selected.

Click Continue for the next step of the tutorial.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step19_Text: As before, click Play to watch your show.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step1_Text:
Learn how to make your own fireworks show.

Note that RollerCoaster Tycoon 3: Soaked! extends fireworks with lasers and water jets, so some buttons and windows have new names - the 'Fireworks MixMaster' is now just the 'MixMaster', for example.

Click the highlighted Scenery button to begin.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step20_Text: Well done, you've reached the end of this tutorial. Keep adding fireworks and bases to your show if you like, and click Quit when you want to leave.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step2_Text: Next, click the highlighted MixMaster button.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step3_Text:
The window now open at the bottom left is the MixMaster. It has all you need to design and schedule fireworks shows.

Click Continue to start learning how it works.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step4_Text: Let's start by loading a ready-made fireworks show. Click the Load a MixMaster show button at the bottom left.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step5_Text: In the new window, click an entry and then Load to open that show. Double clicking a file loads it too.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step6_Text:
A set of firework bases now follows your mouse pointer. Fireworks are launched from these.

Find a good spot on the ground and left click to place them.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step7_Text:
The big window now open is the MixMaster Sequencer, where you watch and edit shows.

Press Play to watch the show you just loaded.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step8_Text: You've seen how to load a show; now let's design one. Click the MixMaster Displays button first.
TutorialText_Fireworks_Step9_Text: Next, click the highlighted Add MixMaster show button.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step10_Text: Lowering ground works just like raising it. Start by picking the Create Canyon tool.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step11_Text:
Put the mouse pointer on the ground and hold the left button until you've dug a fairly deep hollow.

You can move the mouse while digging to spread the canyon over a wider area.

Click Continue when done.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step12_Text:
Smoothing tools flatten the ground, which helps when placing rides and scenery. There is an automatic flatten tool, but flattening by hand gives you more control.

Like the other ground tools, the brush size sets how much ground the tool affects.

Click the highlighted smooth terrain button at the bottom left of the screen.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step13_Text:
Before flattening anything, here are the tools on offer:

'Terrain averager' evens out differences between neighbouring tiles. It does not make the ground flat, but it can make slopes gentler.

'Flatten to height at pointer' levels the area around to the height of the tile under the mouse pointer.

'Flatten in increments for rides and scenery' makes flat ground ready for rides and scenery.

'Flatten terrain' levels the chosen area.

'Change smooth terrain to reveal tile edges' makes upright steps at the edges of the chosen tiles.

'Remove exposed terrain edges' undoes the tool before it.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step14_Text:
Let's flatten some ground with the flatten terrain tool. When flattening for rides, paths or scenery, use 'flatten in increments for rides and scenery' instead.

Click the highlighted flatten terrain tool button.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step15_Text:
Move the brush over something you built earlier (the mountain, say) and hold the left mouse button to flatten it.

Press Continue when you want the next step.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step16_Text: Up to now we've used the 'spray' mode for shaping ground, but there is also a 'drag' mode. Click the highlighted Mode button to switch.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step17_Text:
This window switches between spray and drag mode. The number beside the spray icon sets how fast spray mode changes the ground.

Let's try drag mode. Rather than just holding the left button as in spray mode, you hold it and move the mouse forwards or backwards to set how strong the tool is.

Pick the highlighted Drag button.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step18_Text: To try drag mode, first pick the Raise terrain button.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step19_Text: Next, pick the Create Mountain button.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step1_Text:
This tutorial introduces the ground tools, advanced path building and wall sets in RollerCoaster Tycoon 3.

Click Continue to begin.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step20_Text:
Put the mouse pointer where you want the mountain and hold the left button. While holding, move the mouse forwards to raise the mountain and backwards to lower it. Let go when it's the height you want.

Make more mountains in drag mode if you like. Press Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step21_Text: You can shape the ground; now let's paint it. Click the terrain textures button highlighted on the left of the screen.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step22_Text: There are two ways to paint the ground. One repaints the underground faces - the upright 'cliff' sides of a tile that some ground tools leave showing. The main tool for ground colors, though, is the highlighted Terrain Surface tool. Click it now.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step23_Text: Let's paint some ground with grass. Click the highlighted grass button.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step24_Text:
Move the brush over the ground and hold the left button to paint. New textures painted over old ones blend in by themselves.

Give it a try, and click Continue once you've painted some ground.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step25_Text:
First, a quick word on water. Click the water button (pulsing on the left of the screen), then click the ground to fill it with water up to that point.

We'll skip that for now, so click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step26_Text:
Now for paths. There are three ways to lay them, starting with freeform mode.

Click the path button to open the paths menu.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step27_Text:
A plain asphalt path is picked to start with. In freeform mode, left click fairly flat ground to lay path, or hold the button to paint path over a wide area. Right click a path to delete it.

Try it, and click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step28_Text:
Now for the second path mode. Zoom in close to a path tile you've laid (or lay a new one if none is near).

Click just inside the edge of that tile. An arrow should appear on the edge, pointing out. If not, try again, clicking just inside the path's edge.

Click Continue once you see an arrow.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step29_Text:
Put the mouse pointer on the arrow, hold the left button and move the mouse forwards. An upward sloping path tile appears and is laid when you let go. Move the mouse backwards instead for a downward slope.

If no sloping tile appears, the ground there may not suit (too bumpy or steep, say). Try again from another path tile.

Play around with this way of building paths, and click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step2_Text: First open the ground tools: click the terrain tools button highlighted on the left of the screen.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step30_Text:
The third way works much like building a coaster, and is called anchored mode.

Lay one path tile, then use the arrow and slope buttons at the bottom left of the screen to extend it. Try it out, and click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step31_Text:
Last, let's look at wall sets: scenery pieces that fit together into big buildings such as houses, castles and temples.

We'll build a simple house. If you think you've gone wrong at any point, don't worry - you can still go on to the next step.

Click the scenery button to start.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step32_Text: Then click the walls, roofs and buildings button.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step33_Text: This is the wall set browser, listing wall sets and their pieces. For our house, click the Brick Walls wall set to see its pieces.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step34_Text:
Pick the 'Brick base wall with door' piece. Its outline now follows the mouse pointer over the ground.

The key thing about wall pieces is that they sit on the edges of ground tiles. Move the piece around to see this.

Place it on flat ground, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step35_Text:
Now pick 'Brick base wall with window' and place it facing the door piece, two tiles back.

Click Continue once it's placed.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step36_Text:
Corner pieces will join the two pieces you've placed. Click 'Brick base wall corner' to pick it.

Use a few corner pieces to join the two walls, then click Continue. Made a mistake? Right click a piece to delete it.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step37_Text: Our little house needs a roof. Pick the full-height block roof in the wall set browser, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step38_Text:
To lift the roof above the walls, hold Shift and move the mouse forwards to raise it off the ground, or backwards to lower it. This works for scenery, and even for rides and shops.

Press Z or click the highlighted rotate button to turn a wall piece.

Place the roof pieces to finish your house, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step39_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step3_Text: Three buttons have appeared. Click the first one, the ground shaping tool.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step4_Text:
The window at the bottom left has every tool you need to reshape your park's ground.

Let's start by raising some ground. Click the highlighted raise terrain button.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step5_Text:
Four tools raise the ground:

Create ridge makes steep slopes.

Create mesa makes steep slopes with a flat top.

Create mountain makes sharp slopes with pointed tops.

Create hill top makes rounded mounds.

Click the highlighted create mountain button first.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step6_Text:
RCT3 shapes ground with the 'spray' method unless you change it. There is also a 'drag' method, covered later in this tutorial.

To raise a mountain with spray, move the mouse pointer over the ground and hold the left button. The longer you hold it in one spot, the stronger the effect. You can move the brush to other spots while holding.

Raise a mountain wherever you like, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step7_Text:
Before lowering ground, a quick look at brush size. At the bottom left of the screen is a blue circle. Hold the left button on it and move the mouse forwards and backwards to resize it. The bigger the circle, the more ground the tools change.

Try changing the brush size and raising a few more mountains. Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step8_Text:
You've raised a mountain; now let's lower the ground by digging a canyon.

Click the highlighted lower terrain button to see the three lowering tools.
TutorialText_Landscaping_Step9_Text:
Before digging, here are the lowering tools:

Create canyon digs hollows with steep sides.

Create crater digs a hollow with a raised rim.

Create trough digs a hollow with gentle sides.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step10_Text: Your new laser must be tied to an emitter. Click the laser in the timeline to select it, then click one of the emitters you placed. Once tied, the red circle at the left end of the effect's bar turns green. Click Continue when the laser is tied to an emitter.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step11_Text:
The MixMaster can now change where an emitter aims while the show runs.

Tick the highlighted box.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step12_Text: A bar has appeared along the top of the MixMaster timeline. Left click it to add an angle control point, and right click a point to remove it. Add one now, above the middle of the laser you just placed, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step13_Text:
Now click the emitter your laser is tied to. Rotation markers appear, showing where it points. Hold the left button and move the mouse around to change the emitter's angle.

Add a few key frames and change the angle at each to point the laser different ways. Zoom in on the emitter if it's hard to aim.

Click Continue when done.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step14_Text:
Add as many angle control points to as many emitters as you want; one point can steer several emitters. With a control point selected, every emitter using it lights up green. With a base or effect selected, the control points it uses light up yellow.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step15_Text:
A few more tips on angle control points:

An emitter always starts out aimed as set by the first control point tied to it, wherever that point sits on the timeline.

Right click a control point to delete it.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step16_Text:
A quick look at water shows. Lasers, fireworks and water jets can share one show, so there's no need to make a new one.

Click the Bases button first.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step17_Text:
Pick the highlighted water jet base and place it on the ground.

Click Continue when done.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step18_Text: Next, click the highlighted MixMaster Sequencer button.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step19_Text: Click an empty spot on the timeline.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step1_Text:
Welcome to the laser show tutorial. RollerCoaster Tycoon 3: Soaked! extends the MixMaster with lasers and water jets alongside fireworks, and all three can share a show.

This tutorial assumes you know the MixMaster basics. If not, see the RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 fireworks tutorial first.

Click the Scenery button to begin.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step20_Text: Click 'Water Jets' to see the ready-made jets.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step21_Text: Pick a water jet from the list: double click it, or click it once and press OK.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step22_Text:
Tie the water jet to the emitter you placed earlier: click the jet, then the emitter.

Click Continue when done.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step23_Text:
Well done - you've finished this tutorial! The MixMaster's Play button is on, so you can watch the show you made.

When you've seen enough, press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step2_Text: Next, click the MixMaster button. (RCT3 used to call it the 'Fireworks' button.)
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step3_Text: Then click the MixMaster Bases button.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step4_Text: This menu has the objects that serve as bases for a show: for fireworks, lasers and water jets. For now we only need the laser emitter. Pick the highlighted laser emitter and place a few on the ground, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step5_Text: Next, click the MixMaster Displays button.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step6_Text: Click the 'Add MixMaster Display' button to make a new show.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step7_Text: Here is the MixMaster timeline. Click anywhere on it to start adding a laser.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step8_Text: The MixMaster palette is open, and now lists laser effects and water jets as well as fireworks. Click 'Lasers' to open the lasers menu.
TutorialText_Lasers1_Step9_Text: Double click a laser effect to add it to the timeline, or click it and press OK. The panel on the right previews the selected laser.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step10_Text: 'Trail persist' sets how much 'afterglow' each beam leaves behind as it moves. Leave it as it is for now and click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step11_Text: 'No. Beams' sets how many beams the emitter fires, spread out in a cone. Raise it to 20, then click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step12_Text:
At the bottom of the window are several timelines. They work like the base angle control points in the last tutorial: drag points along, left click an empty spot to add one, right click one to delete it.

Try adding a control point on the Color timeline.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step13_Text:
This is the color window. Set the laser's red, green and blue amounts here; the fourth bar sets how bright it is.

Click OK to close the window when you're happy with the color.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step14_Text: To change how fast the cone of beams turns, click the control point on the 'Rotation speed' timeline, or add a new one there.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step15_Text:
This is the rotation speed window. Click the up/down arrows to change the speed, or hold the left button on the picture in the middle and move the mouse left or right.

Set it to 1 radian per second, then click OK.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step16_Text: To change the angle the beams leave the emitter at, click the control point on the 'Elevation' timeline, or add a new one there.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step17_Text: This is the elevation window, which works like the rotation speed one. Set the elevation to 1.0 radians and watch the preview change. Click OK to close the window.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step18_Text: The last timeline sets beam width. Click its control point, or add a new one.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step19_Text: This is the beam width window, which sets how sharp each beam is. Try 1.3, then click OK.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step1_Text:
Welcome to the Advanced Laser Designer tutorial. RollerCoaster Tycoon 3: Soaked! comes with tools for making laser shows of your own.

Click the Scenery button to begin.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step20_Text: Save your laser now so you can use it in the park. Click the 'Save Laser' button.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step21_Text: Give your laser a file name (ending in '.las') and click Save.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step22_Text: Last, let's load your laser into the park to see it at its best. Close the Advanced Laser Designer with the highlighted close button.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step23_Text: Next, click on the MixMaster timeline.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step24_Text: Find your saved laser in the list and double click it to load it.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step25_Text:
There are laser emitters dotted around this park. Tie your laser to one as usual, then click Play to watch your show.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step26_Text:
Before we finish, a few handy tips:

Double click a laser on the MixMaster timeline to edit it in the Advanced Laser Designer.

Hold Ctrl and drag any effect (laser, firework or water jet) on the timeline to copy it.

There is also an Advanced Water Jet designer that works like the laser one.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step27_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Click Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step4_Text: Left click anywhere on the MixMaster timeline to open the effects palette.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step6_Text: Click 'Advanced Laser Designer' to start designing a laser
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step7_Text:
There are several kinds of laser effect, each giving the beams a different shape; this tutorial sticks to 'Cone of Light'.

First, click the text box and type a name for your laser. Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step8_Text: Use the up/down arrows right of 'Duration' to set how long the effect lasts, or hold the left button on the number and move the mouse up and down to change it quickly. Set about 20 seconds, then click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Lasers2_Step9_Text: Set the laser's power the same way as its duration. Power decides how far the beams reach before fading out. Watch the effect's cost change as you adjust this and other settings. Set the power to about 400, then click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step10_Text: This is the 'sketch pad' for drawing your own pictures. Click and drag the mouse pointer around the window to draw. Click the bin icon to wipe it if you don't like it. Click Continue when you're happy with your drawing.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step11_Text: Now click the green tick to confirm your drawing.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step12_Text: Time to save the laser. Give it a name, then click the Save Laser button.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step13_Text: Type a file name for your laser and click Save.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step14_Text: Close the Advanced Laser Designer with the highlighted close button.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step15_Text: Then click on the MixMaster timeline.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step16_Text: Find your saved laser in the list and double click it to load it.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step17_Text:
There is a laser emitter in this park next to a big wall. Tie your laser to it as usual.

Click Continue when done.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step18_Text: Now aim the emitter at the wall so your picture is drawn on it. Tick the aiming controls box first.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step19_Text:
The aiming line has appeared. Click its far left end to place a control point, click the emitter to use that point, then hold the left button on the emitter and move the mouse to aim it.

Once it points at the wall, click Play to see your laser. If it misses, keep adjusting with the aiming controls.

Click Continue when you want to end this tutorial.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step1_Text:
Welcome to the picture-drawing lasers tutorial. Here you'll learn to make lasers that draw pictures onto a surface.

Click the Scenery button to begin.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step20_Text:
Before we finish, a few more handy tips:

Each frame of your laser can have its own duration.

The drawing editor can load and save single frames.

The laser designer's 'Scale' option makes your picture bigger or smaller.

Right click a drawing frame in the laser designer to delete it from the sequence.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step21_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Click Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step4_Text: Left click anywhere on the MixMaster timeline to open the effects palette.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step6_Text: Click 'Advanced Laser Designer' to start designing a laser
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step7_Text: The laser type needs changing. Click the words 'Cone of light' and pick 'Persisting Image' from the drop-down list.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step8_Text:
The Advanced Laser Designer now looks different. You can still change things like duration and color, but leave them for now.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Lasers3_Step9_Text: Near the bottom of the window is a row of gray and black boxes: the frames of your laser picture, drawn one after another from left to right. Click the first frame to start editing it.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step10_Text:
Wherever you click on the MixMaster timeline, the trick you add lands on its bottom line, which is kept for lion tricks. Several tricks snap together with no gaps.

Lion and tiger tricks last much longer than effects like fireworks, so zooming the timeline out can help. Try it: click the highlighted 'minus' icon at the bottom right of the window once.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step11_Text:
How exciting your lion show is (and so the highest entry fee you can ask) depends on how many tricks there are, how varied and how good they are, and whether other MixMaster effects such as fireworks join in.

Click Play to watch the lion show.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step12_Text:
Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Every button you need is on if you want to watch your show and add more tricks.

Click Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step1_Text:
Welcome to the lion show tutorial. You'll learn to build a lion show and set up the lions' tricks.

All of it applies to the tiger show as well. If you have RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Soaked! and have built whale or dolphin shows there, you can skip this tutorial: lion and tiger shows work the same way.

Click the Rides button to begin.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step2_Text: Next, click the Gentle Rides button.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step3_Text: Pick the Lion Show from the list. (You may have to scroll and/or use the expand/collapse button.)
TutorialText_LionShow_Step4_Text: Move the mouse pointer to where you want the show and left click to place it.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step5_Text: Now place the entrance and exit, just like any other ride: click once for the entrance and again somewhere else for the exit.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step6_Text: Unless you change it, a lion or tiger show runs a random mix of whichever moves and tricks have been researched. You can also set the lions' routine yourself: click the highlighted 'Safari MixMaster' button.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step7_Text:
The MixMaster timeline is open. Add the lion show's moves and tricks here. You can also tie fireworks to the show (and lasers and water jets, with RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Soaked!). The lions do one trick at a time, so their tricks only go on the bottom bar of the timeline - the one with trees behind it.

Click on the timeline to start adding a lion trick.
TutorialText_LionShow_Step9_Text: These are the lion tricks you have right now. In most parks not every trick is there at the start - the rest must be researched. Double click a trick to add it to the MixMaster timeline.
TutorialText_Management_Step10_Text:
The highlighted drop-down box picks what information is shown: status, popularity, satisfaction, weekly profit, queue length, queue time, reliability, downtime and guests' favourite.

Close the attractions window for the next step of the tutorial.
TutorialText_Management_Step11_Text:
Click the research button to open the research window. Here you pay to develop new things for your park. The bar beside each area sets how much it matters.

Close the research window for the next step of the tutorial.
TutorialText_Management_Step12_Text: The staff window is where you manage the people working in your park. Click the staff button to open it.
TutorialText_Management_Step13_Text: The window lists all your staff. The sort drop-down sets the order, anything from job to laziness.
TutorialText_Management_Step14_Text:
Double click a worker's icon in the list to pick them. Their own panel opens at the bottom right of the screen. Give it a try.

Each worker's panel has these same controls; open it by clicking their icon as before, or by clicking them in the park.
TutorialText_Management_Step15_Text: Left click the expand icon to see a worker in more detail. From there you can see more about them and act on it: change their pay, train them, give them jobs, set patrol areas, warn them and change their uniform.
TutorialText_Management_Step16_Text: You can also hire new staff in the staff window. The second tutorial covered that, so we'll skip it here.
TutorialText_Management_Step17_Text:
The show staff buttons filter which workers are listed; grayed-out kinds are hidden. Shop and stall vendors are hidden to start with. Click the show vendors button to list them.

Close the staff window for the next step of the tutorial.
TutorialText_Management_Step18_Text:
The finances window shows how your park's money is doing.

Click the financial management button to open it.
TutorialText_Management_Step19_Text: The finances window has two parts and opens on the monthly summary, which shows income and costs month by month, along with your cash and the value of the park and company.
TutorialText_Management_Step1_Text: This tutorial introduces running your park. We'll go through the controls and options you have, with some tips on running a park well.
TutorialText_Management_Step20_Text: Turn the loan spinner to pay back your loan or borrow more. How much you can borrow, and at what interest, depends on the scenario.
TutorialText_Management_Step21_Text: The second part of the finances window holds graphs. Click the graphs button to open it.
TutorialText_Management_Step22_Text:
The graphs show how your finances change over time.

Close the finances window for the next step of the tutorial.
TutorialText_Management_Step23_Text:
The park operations window gathers many controls for your park.

Click the park operations button to open it.
TutorialText_Management_Step24_Text:
The park operations window opens on land and status. Here you can rename the park and open or close it. Where the scenario allows, you can also set the entry fee and buy land, and in some scenarios buy building rights to build over certain areas.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_Management_Step25_Text: Click the value, ratings and attendance button to see the park graphs.
TutorialText_Management_Step26_Text:
The graphs track park figures live, such as park rating, publicity and guest count. Tick the box next to a figure to see it.

Then click the marketing campaigns button.
TutorialText_Management_Step27_Text:
Marketing campaigns bring more guests to your park - though it helps to have a park worth visiting first! Click an option in the list to start a campaign; running campaigns are listed here too.

Click the awards button to open the awards panel.
TutorialText_Management_Step28_Text: Awards you win are listed in the awards panel. Depending on the scenario there are many to win, such as tidiest park or best food. Awards help your finances too - but watch out, there are bad awards as well, and they can bring fines.
TutorialText_Management_Step29_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Management_Step2_Text: In career mode or a custom scenario, keep your goals in mind. Click the scenario goals button any time to check them; try it now. (It sits on the left of the bar along the top of the screen.)
TutorialText_Management_Step3_Text: The scenario goals are also in the park management menu (more on that menu in the next part). Either button opens the scenario goals window, which lists what you must do to reach Apprentice, Entrepreneur or Tycoon. A finished goal gets a tick next to it.
TutorialText_Management_Step4_Text: Close the scenario goals window and we'll get on with running your park.
TutorialText_Management_Step5_Text:
Every window for running your park is in the park management menu. Next we'll look at each window in turn.

Click the park management button to open the menu.
TutorialText_Management_Step6_Text: The attractions window lists every ride, shop and facility in your park. Click the attractions button to open it.
TutorialText_Management_Step7_Text: The window starts by listing your rides. Click the shops button to see shops.
TutorialText_Management_Step8_Text: Here are the shops in your park. Click the facilities button to see facilities.
TutorialText_Management_Step9_Text: Here are the facilities. Click the name or status button to sort the list, and click again to reverse it. Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step10_Text:
The pool paths window also has buttons for ramps and spiral staircases; a later tutorial covers those.
Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step11_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial and know the basics of building a pool! The advanced pools tutorial shows how to let guests in and keep pools clean. Press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step1_Text:
Welcome to RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Soaked! This expansion adds new rides, scenery and features, and a set of new tutorials introduces them. The tutorials from the original RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3 are still available.

This tutorial shows how to build a simple swimming pool. Click the Rides icon to begin.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step2_Text: Next, click the Swimming Pools icon.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step3_Text:
To make a pool, hold the left mouse button down on the ground and drag. A see-through 'ghost' of the pool appears. Let go of the button and the pool is built.

Click Continue once you've made a pool.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step4_Text:
Drag new pool tiles over or beside the pool to make it bigger. There are several corner shapes - pick the highlighted 'Diagonals' button and add a few more pieces.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step5_Text:
Now pick the highlighted 'Loose curves' button and add some more pieces. Clicking existing pool tiles replaces them.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step6_Text: See the tiled areas around the pool? Click the Place Tiles icon to add more. Try it now.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step7_Text: Add some tiled areas around the edge of the pool, then click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step8_Text:
The grid icon is now highlighted. It shows or hides the grid, handy when building pools above the ground.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_Pools1_Step9_Text:
Click the highlighted Paths icon. It lets you join paths to the edges of tiled areas to link pools together. Click the edge of a pool complex, then build some paths with the usual path tools.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step10_Text:
The changing room's second job is keeping the pools clean. Pools get dirty as guests use them. Each time a mechanic inspects the changing room, they top up the cleaning fluid in its pool filter.

Every top-up costs money, and every changing room keeps its own tank of fluid. With several changing rooms, inspecting each less often can cut the cost of fluid.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step11_Text:
There are three cleaning fluids. The standard one should do for a medium pool if your mechanics top it up often enough. If you get warnings that pools are too dirty, have mechanics visit more often or switch to a stronger fluid.

Adding another changing room works much like inspecting more often, since each has its own fluid tank and inspection interval.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step12_Text: Before we finish, a look at pools on several levels. Close the changing room window first with the close button at the bottom right of the screen.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step13_Text: Open the pool building window with the highlighted icon.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step14_Text: Next, click the highlighted 'Toggle Height' icon.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step15_Text:
Click the up arrow to raise the height new pools are built at. Set it to 10 and build a new pool level. You can also hold Shift and drag the mouse to set the height.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step16_Text:
Pool levels can be joined with pool paths or spiral staircases, and neighbouring pools only a little apart in height can be joined with ramps. Let's build a spiral staircase.

Click the Paths button first.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step17_Text: Next, click the highlighted Spiral Staircase button.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step18_Text:
Move the mouse over a fully paved pool tile. Where the staircase fits, the preview turns blue. Hold the left button, drag the mouse up and down to set its height, and let go to place it.

The pool tile buttons are on, in case you want more pool areas to join with staircases.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step19_Text: Mouse gestures make waves and whirlpools in your pools. To try them, first close the pool building window with the close button at the bottom left of the screen.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step1_Text: Welcome to the advanced pools tutorial. You'll learn how to let guests into your pool, keep pools clean, and more. Click Continue to begin.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step20_Text:
With the mouse pointer over a pool, hold the left button and move the mouse as if drawing a circle in the water. Keep circling for a few seconds, then let go. If it worked, a whirlpool appears. If not, try again - it can take practice.

Draw lines in the water to make waves too.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step21_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! The next one shows how to add water slides to your pool. Press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step2_Text:
In front of you is a pool complex: pools, tiles and paths all joined up. It can be a single pool or many, as long as tiles or paths join them.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step3_Text: Every pool complex needs at least one changing room, or guests can't get into the pools. Let's add one. To open the pool window, click Rides first.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step5_Text: Click the highlighted icon to open the changing rooms window.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step6_Text: Pick any changing room, then click beside the pool's edge to add it.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step7_Text: Open the changing room: click the 'Open or Close' button, then the green button.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step8_Text: Well done - the pool complex is open and guests will start using it. Now for some key jobs the changing room does. Click the highlighted Finances button.
TutorialText_Pools2_Step9_Text:
As with other attractions, the Finances window sets what guests pay to enter your pool complex. The better the complex, the more you can charge. Its size, layout, extras and rides all count towards how good it is.

Click the Maintenance button to go on.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step10_Text:
Hold Shift to raise the station piece to the height of one of the pool's raised platforms, and place it right beside the platform.

Don't worry if it's hard to line up - in the game there are several ways to join pools to pool rides, and pool paths are especially handy.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step11_Text:
Use the usual track tools to steer the slide down towards the main pool. When it's done, make sure the last piece is level (neither climbing nor falling), then pick the Flume End piece from the specials list on the right.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step12_Text: Close the building window with the close button at the bottom left of the screen.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step13_Text: Test the ride as usual: click the red flag button, then the amber button.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step14_Text:
Well done - you've finished this tutorial!

The body slide's Open button is on if you want to watch guests use it, and so is the test results button, to see how exciting it is.

Press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step1_Text:
Welcome to the pool facilities tutorial. You'll learn to add pool extras and pool rides. They make the pool more fun for guests and let you charge more to use it.

Click Rides to begin.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step3_Text: Click Extras to start building pool extras.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step4_Text: Each kind of pool extra has to go in a certain kind of spot. Spa pools, showers and sun loungers, for example, go on fully paved pool tiles. Place a spa pool now, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step5_Text: Ladders and small diving boards go on the edge of a pool. Place a few, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step6_Text: Large diving boards go on a raised platform. Place one, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step7_Text:
Now for pool rides such as water slides. Guests reach these from the pools, not through the usual entrance and exit.

First close the pool window with the close button at the bottom left of the screen.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step8_Text: Next, click the 'Pool Slides and Rides' button.
TutorialText_Pools3_Step9_Text: Pick Body Slide from the list. (You may have to scroll to find it.)
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step10_Text: Click the Sold Items button to start choosing what your stall sells.
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step11_Text:
Use the '<Select stall type>' drop-down list to pick which stall your custom stall copies. It then works just like any other stall in the game, and you can change what it sells whenever you like.

Close the stall window with the close button at the bottom right of the screen when you want the next step.
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step12_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step1_Text:
This updated RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3 includes some features from the Wild! expansion, such as billboards and the custom stall. This tutorial shows how to use them.

Click Continue to begin.
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step2_Text: Billboards make your park feel more real and bring in a little extra money. With an internet connection, the adverts update themselves now and then. You can also make billboards with your own pictures. Click the highlighted Scenery button to start placing one.
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step4_Text:
This window lists every advert on offer, with the Custom Image option at the top. Billboards are placed like any scenery: click a picture to pick an advert, pick a billboard type and place it on the ground. Without an internet connection there are no adverts to place.

When you want to go on, click Custom Image to learn how to put your own pictures in the park.
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step5_Text:
This window lists what's in your My Pictures folder. Click a picture to make a billboard from it; billboard types appear on the right. Pick one and place it on the ground. (Press Z to turn the billboard before placing it.)

The 'Queue Image' button puts several pictures on one billboard, which shows them one after another.

Place a few custom pictures, then close the billboard list when you want to go on.
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step6_Text:
Also new is the custom stall, a flexible stall that can act like any other stall in the game. You could, say, make it sell what a balloon stall sells and later switch it to burgers. Custom stalls can also carry billboards.

Click the Shops & Facilities button to start placing one.
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step8_Text: Find 'Custom stall' in the list and click it.
TutorialText_RCT3GoldExtras_Step9_Text: Place the stall on the ground wherever you like.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step10_Text: Click the Sold Items button to start choosing what your stall sells.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step11_Text:
Use the '<Select stall type>' drop-down list to pick which stall your custom stall copies. It then works just like any other stall in the game, and you can change what it sells whenever you like.

Close the stall window with the close button at the bottom right of the screen when you want the next step.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step12_Text: Time to make a waterfall. Click the highlighted Terrain Tools button to start.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step14_Text:
To make a waterfall, click the two bodies of water you want to join. Try it with the ones in this park.

Click Continue once you've made a waterfall this way.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step15_Text: With the waterfall tool still picked, right click a waterfall to delete it. Try it, then click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step16_Text:
Players of RollerCoaster Tycoon® 1 and 2 may remember building coasters and paths through cliff faces to make tunnels. Now RCT3 can do it too.

Click the highlighted Rides button to try it.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step18_Text: Pick the LIM Launched Coaster from the list. (This coaster needs no lift hills, as it is launched by motors.)
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step19_Text:
The coaster building and testing tools are on. Place the first piece on open ground as usual and build a station as normal. For a tunnel, just build the coaster into a hill or cliff face. The ground turns see-through while you build underground so you can see your work.

Click Continue when you've finished trying out tunnels.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step1_Text:
This updated RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3 includes some features from the Soaked! and Wild! expansions, such as waterfalls, tunnels, billboards and the custom stall. This tutorial shows how to use them.

Click Continue to begin.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step20_Text:
Before we go on, a few more tips on tunnels:

The ride's Vehicles window sets whether underground track pieces have lights, and their color.

Paths can be built underground too.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step21_Text:
Several new items go on path edges:

Jumping fountains - they shoot little jets of water to each other in different patterns.

Loudspeakers - they play music anywhere, and also come as scenery for tiles without path.

Passport machines - a guest who visits enough of them gets a free souvenir.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step22_Text: The Ctrl key now helps you place scenery at a set height. Click the highlighted Scenery button to try it.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step24_Text:
Pick any scenery item and place a few on the ground. Place some at different heights by holding Shift and moving the mouse up and down before placing.

Now try holding Ctrl, which does two things. Normally it places the next item at the height of the last one. And if you press Ctrl with the mouse pointer over a scenery item, then next time you hold Ctrl the new piece goes at the height of that 'picked' one.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step25_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step2_Text: Billboards make your park feel more real and bring in a little extra money. With an internet connection, the adverts update themselves now and then. You can also make billboards with your own pictures. Click the highlighted Scenery button to start placing one.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step4_Text:
This window lists every advert on offer, with the Custom Image option at the top. Billboards are placed like any scenery: click a picture to pick an advert, pick a billboard type and place it on the ground. Without an internet connection there are no adverts to place.

When you want to go on, click Custom Image to learn how to put your own pictures in the park.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step5_Text:
This window lists what's in your My Pictures folder. Click a picture to make a billboard from it; billboard types appear on the right. Pick one and place it on the ground. (Press Z to turn the billboard before placing it.)

The 'Queue Image' button puts several pictures on one billboard, which shows them one after another.

Place a few custom pictures, then close the billboard list when you want to go on.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step6_Text:
Also new is the custom stall, a flexible stall that can act like any other stall in the game. You could, say, make it sell what a balloon stall sells and later switch it to burgers. Custom stalls can also carry billboards.

Click the Shops & Facilities button to start placing one.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step8_Text: Find 'Custom stall' in the list and click it.
TutorialText_RCT3JewelExtras_Step9_Text: Place the stall on the ground wherever you like.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step10_Text: Click the Autocomplete button to accept its answer.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step11_Text: The game now asks for the ride's entrance and exit. We only want to test this ride, so skip that with the close button at the bottom left of the screen.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step12_Text: Click the red flag button, then the amber button, to put the ride into test mode.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step13_Text:
Well done - you've finished this tutorial! All the buttons for CoasterCam are on if you want to see the enclosure the way a guest would.

Click Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step1_Text:
Welcome to the safari transport tutorial. You'll learn to build a transport ride that runs through an animal enclosure.

Click the Rides button to begin.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step2_Text: Next, click the Transport Rides button.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step3_Text: Three transport rides can pass through enclosures: Safari Transport, Safari Train and Elephant Transport. This time we'll build the Safari Transport. Find it in the list and click it.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step4_Text: Place the first station piece on the glowing tile on the ground.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step5_Text: Click the station button twice to make the station long enough.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step6_Text: Next, click the straight piece button three times.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step7_Text:
A gate has replaced the enclosure fence there, letting the vehicle into the enclosure.

Click the right medium curve button three times to go on.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step8_Text: Let Autocomplete finish the track: click the Autocomplete button.
TutorialText_SafariTransport_Step9_Text: Wait while the game works out how to finish the track. The autocomplete button flashes when it's done; then click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial1_Step1_Text:
This tutorial shows how to get around your parks with the 3D camera. Think of it as a TV or film camera you control completely.

RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 has several camera control modes; this tutorial covers Normal mode, which has been switched on for you. See the manual for the others.

Click Continue to begin.
TutorialText_Tutorial1_Step2_Text:
To look left and right, turning the camera, hold the mouse wheel (or both mouse buttons) and move the mouse left and right.

To move the camera across your park, hold the right mouse button and move the mouse the way you want to go. The arrow keys move the camera too. The camera keeps the same height above the ground, so it follows hills and dips.

Try these, then click Continue for the next step.

Note: the camera won't move while the mouse pointer is over a window.
TutorialText_Tutorial1_Step3_Text:
You can also move the camera by pushing the mouse pointer against the top, bottom, left or right edge of the screen; the camera moves that way.

(This only works when the game runs full screen.)

Try it, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Tutorial1_Step4_Text:
To tilt the camera up or down for a moment, hold the mouse wheel (or both mouse buttons) and move the mouse backwards or forwards. Let go and the camera goes back to its usual angle.

Try it, then click Continue for the next part.
TutorialText_Tutorial1_Step5_Text:
Roll the mouse wheel backwards and forwards to zoom the camera in and out.

The Page Up and Page Down keys zoom too.

Try it, then click Continue.
TutorialText_Tutorial1_Step6_Text:
Time for the thrill of CoasterCam! You may have spotted a coaster in this park.

Move the camera to its track and click any part of it to open the coaster's panel.
TutorialText_Tutorial1_Step7_Text:
There are two ways into CoasterCam: click the coaster's Details button and then the camera icon, or double click the round picture of the ride's train.

Use either one to enter CoasterCam now.
TutorialText_Tutorial1_Step8_Text:
Move the mouse pointer while in CoasterCam to bring up its menu.

On CoasterCam, hold the left mouse button and move the mouse to look around. Roll the mouse wheel to move the camera nearer to or further from where it is mounted.

The Next Train button switches trains.

When you've had enough, press the Leave CoasterCam button.
TutorialText_Tutorial1_Step9_Text:
Well done, you now have all the camera skills to enjoy RollerCoaster Tycoon in 3D!  With a little practice, viewing anything in your parks from any angle will come naturally.

Look around and play with the 3D camera, then click Quit when you want to end this tutorial.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step10_Text:
