The window at the bottom left is for building paths. There are several ways to build them; for now we'll stick to 'freeform'.

Let's start by giving the coaster a queue.

Click the highlighted queue path button at the bottom left.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step11_Text: Now pick a style of queue path. Click the highlighted queue path button.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step12_Text:
Start with a queue tile in front of the coaster's entrance, which sits beside the station and has a booth and a gate. Click in front of it to place the tile.

Then click beside that tile to make the queue longer, and keep going until it's as long as you want.

If you go wrong, right click a path tile to delete it.

Green arrows may show up on the queue as you build. Ignore them for now - they belong to another way of building paths, covered in a later tutorial.

Click Continue once your queue is done.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step13_Text:
Next, join the coaster's entrance and exit to the park's main path.

Click the regular path button first.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step14_Text: Click the highlighted path type button to pick a style of path.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step15_Text:
Regular paths are placed just like queues. Join the ride's exit, and the end of the queue, to the park's main path.

If you can't see the main path, zoom out with the Page Down key.

Click Continue once the paths are joined up.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step16_Text: Before going on, click Paths to close the path tools.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step17_Text:
The park needs staff to keep it running and clean. Let's hire some.

First open the park management menu, highlighted on the left.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step19_Text:
Let's hire a mechanic first. Mechanics keep the park running by repairing rides, shops and other attractions.

Click the highlighted Hire Mechanic button in the staff window.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step1_Text:
This tutorial shows how to place rides and shops, build paths and hire staff.

Click Continue to begin.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step20_Text:
The mechanic is now on the staff list, and is also hanging in the air waiting for you to put them in the park!

Move the mouse to position them and click to drop them on the ground. Once down, they look for work by themselves.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step21_Text:
In the staff window you can warn and fire staff, train them to improve their skills, and change their pay. The park management and research tutorial covers the staff window in more depth.

Close the staff window with the close button at its top right, or by clicking the Staff button again.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step22_Text:
The worker's panel at the bottom right of the screen also manages one worker at a time and shows their details.

Click the Statistics button at the bottom right to see an example.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step23_Text:
The statistics window shows what your worker has been up to. Every kind of person in the game has a window like this.

Close the worker's panel with the close button at the bottom right when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step24_Text:
Time to open the coaster you built so guests can ride it.

Click any part of the coaster to open its panel.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step25_Text: Click the amber flag icon, then the green button, to open the coaster.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step26_Text:
Your coaster is open; now let's give the park more variety. Not every guest wants fast coasters. Some want something gentler, like the Floundering Ferry.

Before building one, close the coaster's panel with the close button at the bottom right.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step27_Text: Next, click the Rides button on the left of the screen.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step29_Text:
Scroll down to the ride called Floundering Ferry and click its picture.

The icons at the top of the screen filter the list by theme.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step2_Text:
Let's place your first coaster, using a ready-made design for now. To learn to build your own, see the 'Building a custom coaster' tutorial.

To pick a ready-made coaster, open the Rides menu first.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step30_Text:
Find a good spot on the ground for the ride. Its outline is blue where it can go and red where it can't.

Left click to place it once you find a spot.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step31_Text:
Now choose where the ride's entrance and exit go.

The window at the bottom left picks a theme for the entrance.

Move the mouse near the ride and an outline of the entrance appears beside it. Left click when it's in a good spot to place the entrance.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step32_Text: Next, place the ride's exit, exactly like the entrance: pick a theme in the window at the bottom left, then click beside the ride to set where the exit goes.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step33_Text: Test the Floundering Ferry just like a coaster: click the flag icon at the bottom right, then the amber button.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step34_Text:
Last time you learned CoasterCam - but it isn't only for coasters; every ride has it! For the Floundering Ferry, click the ride's Details button, then the camera icon.

Or double click the round picture of the ride at the bottom right of the screen.

Start the Floundering Ferry's CoasterCam now.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step35_Text:
As before, drag with the left mouse button to look around, and use the camera button to switch views.

Click the Leave CoasterCam button at the bottom right of the screen when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step36_Text:
A good park also needs shops and facilities. Let's build a hot dog stall.

Click the highlighted Shops and Facilities button on the left of the screen.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step38_Text: Find the Hot Dog stall in the list and click its picture.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step39_Text:
Find a good spot for the hot dog stall. Shops and facilities must sit right beside a path so customers can reach them.

Once you have a spot by a path, make sure the stall faces the path. Turn it with the Rotate button at the bottom left, or press Z.

Left click to place the stall when you're happy with it.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step40_Text:
Guests can't buy food until the shop is open. Unlike rides, shops need no test first.

Click the flag button, then the green button, to open the shop.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step41_Text:
Your shop is open! Last of all, open the Floundering Ferry and build paths and queues for it. Every button you need is on:

Path and queue buttons are under Paths on the left of the screen.

To open the Floundering Ferry, click it and use the flag button.

The CoasterCam buttons are on too.

This tutorial is finished. Click Quit when you want to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step4_Text:
We'll use a ready-made wooden coaster, so scroll down the coaster list and pick the 'Build a saved track design' button for the Wooden Coaster.

The buttons at the bottom of the window filter the list by coaster type.  The magnifying glass button at the top shrinks the list so more rides fit at once.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step5_Text: Pick the design called 'Little Beast', then click the 'Build this' button.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step6_Text:
An outline of the coaster you picked now follows the mouse; the changed pointer shows you are placing an object.

A blue outline means the coaster can go there. A red one means you must move it until it turns blue. A coaster can't be placed where there isn't room for all of it or the land isn't yours.

Click the rotate button or press Z to turn the coaster.

Left click to place it when you're happy with where it is.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step7_Text:
Now test the coaster. Coasters and some other rides must be tested before guests can ride them: the test checks that the ride works and shows its excitement, intensity and nausea ratings.

Click the flag button, then the amber button, to put the coaster into test mode.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step8_Text:
With the coaster in test mode, you can watch the train go round. While it tests, we'll build paths and queues so guests can reach it.

First close the coaster's panel with the close button at the bottom right of the screen.
TutorialText_Tutorial2_Step9_Text:
Before guests can ride your coaster, it needs queue paths to the entrance, normal paths from the exit, and to be set to 'open'.

Click the Paths button.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step10_Text: Click the medium slope button twelve times to build the lift hill.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step11_Text: Now level the track off, ready for the drop. Click the highlighted button to switch from an upward slope to flat, then click it again to place the piece.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step12_Text: Click the chain again to turn it off, so we can build the drop from normal pieces.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step13_Text: Click the medium slope down button twice to start the drop.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step14_Text: Now go steep for some extra speed. Click the highlighted button four times to add three steep slopes. (Remember - the first click picks the piece, each click after places one.)
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step15_Text: Next, ease into a medium slope.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step16_Text: Finish the drop with a flat straight.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step17_Text:
Now let's add a turn. Any curve would fit, but the cars have picked up speed on the drop, so a plain curve could be rough. Banking the curve eases the forces on riders, and gentle or medium curves pull fewer G's than tight ones.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step18_Text: Let's start the banked curve: click the highlighted 'Flat to Bank' button.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step19_Text: Click the straight button to place the banked straight.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step1_Text:
Last time you placed a ready-made coaster. Now it's your turn to design one!

Click the Rides button on the left of the screen to begin.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step20_Text: Now the turn. Our drop isn't very high, so a medium curve will do. Add two medium curves so the track turns right back round.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step21_Text: Now level out the banking: click the straight button.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step22_Text: Then click the no banking button.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step23_Text: Last, click the straight button to place a straight that leaves the bank.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step24_Text:
Photo sections are special pieces that photograph riders as they pass. With the Allow RollerCoaster Photos option on (it is unless you changed it), a custom family riding the coaster gets photographed at the photo section and the picture is saved to your computer.

Click the photo section button twice to place one now.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step25_Text:
Our coaster doesn't need brakes, but let's look at them quickly: on bigger coasters they help tame extreme G-forces.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step26_Text:
Brakes are special straight pieces that slow the coaster to a speed you choose.

Click Continue for the next step of the tutorial.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step27_Text:
Block brakes are a special kind of brake. As well as slowing the coaster, they make trains stop and wait when the coaster runs several trains.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step28_Text:
Special pieces differ from coaster to coaster and add excitement to a design. They include corkscrews, loops, helixes and S-bends.

You'll find them all on the right of the building window.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step29_Text: The Wooden Coaster has a loop among its special pieces. It needs an upward medium slope first; click the highlighted button twice to place one.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step30_Text:
Some special pieces, like the loop, come in left and right versions. Pick the one you want from the special pieces list - for a right-hand piece, the entry with the right-pointing arrow beside it.

Click the right loop twice to place a loop.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step31_Text: Click the highlighted button to place a flat straight.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step32_Text:
You could finish the coaster by hand, but there is also an autocomplete tool that tries to fill in the rest of your design. Some designs can't be completed, and the tool may take a while to find an answer.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step33_Text: Let's try it. Click the highlighted autocomplete button.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step34_Text: The game now looks for a way to finish the track; with our design it should be quick. Click Continue once the autocomplete tool stops searching.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step35_Text:
When autocomplete is done, it shows the track it suggests. Click the autocomplete button again to accept it.

Click the autocomplete button while it is still searching to stop it. To turn down its answer, click the delete button or any track piece icon in the building window.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step36_Text: Now place the coaster's entrance and exit: click once for the entrance and again for the exit. Move the mouse to where you want each one before clicking.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step37_Text:
The track is complete, but now and then you'll want to swap a piece. If the coaster takes a corner too fast, for example, you could swap the straight before it for a brake.

To swap a piece, click the track piece you want to change and pick its replacement. The demolish icon deletes the selected piece.

We won't do it now, but it's worth remembering.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step38_Text:
There's a second way, handy for rebuilding parts of a coaster.

After clicking a piece, zoom in close and you'll see an arrow showing which way you are building. Placing a piece replaces the current one and moves on to the next.

Click the other end of a piece to build the other way.

Press Continue for the next step of this tutorial.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step39_Text: The coaster is finished. Before we look at running it, let's give it some color. Click the vehicles button.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step3_Text:
To start building a custom coaster, scroll down to the Wooden Coaster and click its picture.

The filter buttons at the bottom of the list hide some kinds of coaster.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step40_Text:
Click one of the paint buckets on the highlighted track color button. Each bucket gives the track one of its three colors.

Try it.

Click Continue when you like the track's colors.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step41_Text: With the coaster complete, it's time to test it. Click the highlighted flag button on the coaster's panel, then the amber button.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step42_Text:
The train now sets off round the track; once it finishes a whole lap the test results appear. Test mode helps fine-tune a design and shows where it doesn't work.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step43_Text: Click the highlighted test results button to see the track's results.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step44_Text:
The test results panel is open. The drop-down box picks which results to show.

Basic results are the excitement, intensity and nausea ratings. Every guest has their own limits for each. Keep intensity and nausea from getting too high or guests won't ride; too low and they'll find it dull.

Speed results show top and average speed, plus ride length and time.

Force results show the highest G-forces on the ride; keep these from getting too high.

Drop results show how many drops there are and the tallest one, plus total airtime and number of inversions.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step45_Text:
Before the coaster controls, a quick look at car types. Most coasters offer more than one, to fit a theme or just give the ride a new look.

Click the vehicles button to change car type.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step46_Text:
The vehicles panel is open. Click the highlighted Change Car Type button to pick another car. Cars often weigh different amounts, and lighter ones are more likely to run out of speed than heavy ones.

Click Continue once you've picked a car type.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step47_Text:
The coaster's panel holds every option for running it. Let's go through each control.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step48_Text:
The graphs panel shows the coaster's speed, height and G-forces live.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step49_Text:
The maintenance panel shows how reliable the coaster is and how long it's been out of action, and can find the nearest mechanic. Have it inspected often to keep it working.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step4_Text:
The window now at the bottom of the screen is for building coasters.

The game stays paused while you build.

There is also a track piece under the mouse pointer. Left click to place it on the glowing tile on the ground. If you can't see the tile, zoom out with Page Down.

You can use the Rotate button (or Z) to set which way it faces before placing it.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step50_Text:
The details panel lets you set music, rename the ride and add entrances or exits. You can also save the coaster design, change the color of any queues joined to it, and use CoasterCam.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step51_Text:
The finances panel sets the ride price and shows the coaster's running costs and profit.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step52_Text:
The guest thoughts panel lists what guests think of the ride.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step53_Text:
The vehicles panel sets the car type and how many cars and trains the coaster has, plus the colors of track and cars.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step54_Text:
The open or close button puts the coaster into test mode, or opens or closes it to guests.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step55_Text:
The test results panel shows all of the coaster's test results.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step56_Text:
The operating mode panel sets how the coaster runs, its waiting rules and the chain lift speed.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step57_Text:
The construction button opens the building window. The game pauses while it is open.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step58_Text:
The customers panel sums up how popular the coaster is with its riders.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step59_Text: To name the coaster, open the details panel first. Click the details button.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step5_Text:
The first piece of the coaster is a station, which every ride needs so guests can get on and off. Most rides need just one; transport rides should have two or more.

The station's length sets how long the coaster's trains can be, so lay several station pieces in a row to make it long enough.

Press Continue to start adding more track.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step60_Text:
Type a new name in the highlighted text box.

Press Continue once you've named the coaster.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step61_Text:
This window can also save your coaster design. Designs are saved by name in the coaster designs folder inside the game's documents folder.

We won't save it this time, so click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step62_Text:
Before ride events, a quick look at deleting a coaster.

The demolish ride button deletes the whole coaster track.

We won't do it now, as we still need this coaster.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step63_Text: Ride events are new in RCT3: staged scenes that add excitement and bold theming to a coaster or tracked ride. They're easy to add, so let's add one.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step64_Text: Click the scenery button, then the ride events button to open the list.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step65_Text: The ride events list shows what's on offer. Click the Oil Derrick and place it anywhere beside our coaster.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step66_Text: Close the ride events list and the preview at the bottom left, then click the Oil Derrick you placed to select it.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step67_Text:
Now set the trigger point: a track piece that starts the event when the train passes over it.

Click the highlighted button, then click the piece of track that should trigger the event.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step68_Text: Last, let's load a saved coaster design. Click the rides button first.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step69_Text: Click the RollerCoasters button to open the coaster list.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step6_Text: Let's add more station pieces. Find the Station button in the building window and click it four times to make four pieces.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step70_Text: Scroll down to the Wooden Coaster and click the folder icon to open its track designs.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step71_Text:
The track design list isn't only ready-made coasters from the RCT3 team - coasters you save show up here too.

Click the cancel button at the bottom right of the list to finish this tutorial.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step72_Text:
Well done - you've reached the end of this tutorial and you're on your way to becoming a master coaster designer!

Click Quit to end the tutorial.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step7_Text:
Next comes a lift hill, the usual way to get trains up a slope, though some coasters have other options such as a powered launch.

Click the Chain button to start building a lift hill.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step8_Text:
Some track pieces are now grayed out because they can't carry a chain. Usually only straight and upward pieces can.

Now click the medium slope button.
TutorialText_Tutorial3_Step9_Text:
A see-through preview of the next piece appears on the coaster.

Click the medium slope button again to place the first piece of the lift hill.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step10_Text: Now close the building window with the close button at the bottom left.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step11_Text: Next, the entrance and exit; click the details button.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step12_Text: With the details panel open, click the place entrance button. Put the entrance on the side nearest land so it's easy to join to the main path, and the exit near it.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step13_Text:
Then build a queue from the entrance to the main path, and a path from the exit to the same path. You may need slopes and ramps to bring the paths to the height of the path on land.

Click Continue once both are joined to the main path.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step14_Text: Nearly there. Before opening the water ride, set how many boats it has. Click the vehicles button to open the vehicles panel.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step15_Text:
Use the number of cars spinner to raise the cars up to, but not past, the number of station pieces you placed.

Click Continue when done.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step16_Text:
Now open the water ride. Like coasters and other rides, it has CoasterCam so you can see what guests see.

Click the flag button, then the green button, to open it.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step17_Text:
RCT3 has a few special rides called stacked rides, such as the Observation Tower, Elevator and Rotodrop.

They usually have a base, plus tower pieces you stack to make the ride as tall as you like. We'll use the Rotodrop.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step18_Text: To build a Rotodrop, click the rides button first.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step19_Text: Click the thrill rides button to open the thrill rides list.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step1_Text:
This tutorial shows how to build water rides and stacked rides in RollerCoaster Tycoon 3.

They are built much like a custom coaster. If you haven't done the custom coaster tutorial yet, we suggest going back to the main menu and doing that one first.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step20_Text: Scroll down the thrill rides list and pick the Rotodrop.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step21_Text: The outline of the Rotodrop's base now shows. Left click the ground where you want it.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step22_Text:
The Rotodrop's building window is open. Click the blue up arrow in the panel to make the ride taller.

Click the highlighted button ten times.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step23_Text:
Just close the building window to finish the Rotodrop; the top piece is added for you.

Click the close button at the bottom left of the screen now.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step24_Text: Click the details button and add an entrance and exit, as for any ride.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step25_Text: Now build queues and paths from the Rotodrop to the main path. Click Continue when done.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step26_Text: As with coasters and tracked rides, test the ride before opening it. Click the flag button, then the amber button, to put the Rotodrop into test mode.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step27_Text: After the ride has done a couple of test runs, click the test results to see how it did. It's now ready to open to guests.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step28_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Click Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step2_Text: Water rides first. These go on water, such as jet skis and rowing boats. Click the rides button to begin.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step3_Text: Then click the water rides button.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step4_Text: The water rides list is open, showing the water rides on offer. We'll use the Jet Skis; click them to pick them.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step5_Text:
With the jet skis picked, the building window has opened at the bottom left of the screen. It works exactly as it does for coasters.

Water rides can be built two ways. The first is as a track, built just like a coaster. The track floats, so there are no slopes, but otherwise it's the same.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step6_Text:
The second way is freer. You place one or more station pieces on the water, and guests then roam the water however they like.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step7_Text: Let's build our first water ride. Make sure the station piece is picked by clicking its icon in the building window.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step8_Text:
An outline of the station piece appears; move it over the water. Place stations with care, since queues and paths must be able to reach them.

Place the station on the glowing tile near the middle of the lake.
TutorialText_WaterRides_Step9_Text:
With one station piece, only one boat can load at a time. Open water rides move guests through slowly, so add a few more station pieces to handle more than one car.

Add two more station pieces now.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step10_Text:
Before we go on, a few more tips on tunnels:

The ride's Vehicles window sets whether underground track pieces have lights, and their color.

Paths can be built underground too.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step11_Text:
Also new: water cannons, which guests use to soak each other.

Click the highlighted Scenery button.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step13_Text:
Water cannons are in the "Other" group. To find them more easily, click the lamps, bins, seats and signs buttons so only "Other" items show.

Pick the Water Cannon and place a few on the edges of the paths in this park. Guests should soon start climbing on and using them.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step14_Text:
Several other new items go on path edges:

Jumping fountains - they shoot little jets of water to each other in different patterns.

Loudspeakers - they play music anywhere, and also come as scenery for tiles without path.

Passport machines - a guest who visits enough of them gets a free souvenir.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step15_Text: The Ctrl key now helps you place scenery at a set height. Click the highlighted Scenery items button to try it.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step16_Text:
Pick any scenery item and place a few on the ground. Place some at different heights by holding Shift and moving the mouse up and down before placing.

Now try holding Ctrl, which does two things. Normally it places the next item at the height of the last one. And if you press Ctrl with the mouse pointer over a scenery item, then next time you hold Ctrl the new piece goes at the height of that 'picked' one.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step17_Text:
Last, a quick look at the water transport ride. Unlike normal transport rides, it sits on water and needs no track except its stations.

Click the highlighted Rides menu to start building one.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step19_Text: Find 'Water Based Transport' in the list and click it.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step1_Text:
This tutorial covers some more new features of RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Soaked!, such as waterfalls, tunnels, water cannons and more.

Click Continue to begin.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step20_Text:
Place the first station piece in the water and add several more - for this ride, stations at least three pieces long work best.

Click Continue once the station is built.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step21_Text: Now place a second station somewhere else. Click the highlighted button left of the track building window; it lets you put the next station piece in a new spot. Try it, and click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step22_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step2_Text: RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Soaked! adds waterfalls. Click the highlighted Terrain Tools button to start making your first one.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step4_Text:
To make a waterfall, click the two bodies of water you want to join. Try it with the ones in this park.

Click Continue once you've made a waterfall this way.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step5_Text: With the waterfall tool still picked, right click a waterfall to delete it. Try it, then click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step6_Text:
Players of RollerCoaster Tycoon® 1 and 2 may remember building coasters and paths through cliff faces to make tunnels. Now RCT3 can do it too.

Click the highlighted Rides button to try it.
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step8_Text: Pick the LIM Launched Coaster from the list. (This coaster needs no lift hills, as it is launched by motors.)
TutorialText_Waterfalls_Step9_Text:
The coaster building and testing tools are on. Place the first piece on open ground as usual and build a station as normal. For a tunnel, just build the coaster into a hill or cliff face. The ground turns see-through while you build underground so you can see your work.

Click Continue when you've finished trying out tunnels.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step10_Text:
Wherever you click on the MixMaster timeline, the move you add lands on its bottom line, which is kept for whale moves. Several moves snap together with no gaps.

Whale and dolphin moves last much longer than effects like lasers, so zooming the timeline out can help. Try it: click the highlighted 'minus' icon at the bottom right of the window once.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step11_Text:
How exciting your whale show is (and so the highest entry fee you can ask) depends on how many moves there are, how varied and how good they are, and whether lasers, fireworks and fountains join in.

Click Play to watch the whale show.

Click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step12_Text:
Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Every button you need is on if you want to watch your show and add more moves.

Click Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step1_Text:
Welcome to the whale show tutorial. You'll learn to build a whale show, choreograph your own routines and mix them with music, fountains, lasers and fireworks.

All of it applies to the dolphin show as well.

Click the Rides button to begin.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step2_Text: Next, click the Gentle Rides button.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step3_Text: Pick the Killer Whale Show from the list. (You may have to scroll and/or use the expand/collapse button.)
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step4_Text: Whale and dolphin shows need water that is deep enough, and there's some ready in this park. Move the mouse pointer over it and click to place the show.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step5_Text: Now place the entrance and exit, just like any other ride: click once for the entrance and again somewhere else for the exit.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step6_Text: Unless you change it, a whale or dolphin show runs a random mix of whichever moves and tricks have been researched. You can also set the whale's routine yourself: click the highlighted 'Aquatic MixMaster' button.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step7_Text:
The MixMaster timeline is open. Add the whale show's moves and tricks here, and tie fireworks, lasers and water jets to it too. The whale does one thing at a time, so its moves only go on the bottom bar of the timeline - the one with waves behind it.

Click on the timeline to start adding a whale move.
TutorialText_WhaleShow_Step9_Text: These are the killer whale moves you have right now. In most parks not every move is there at the start - the rest must be researched. Double click a move to add it to the MixMaster timeline.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step10_Text: Place the first station piece inside the glowing area on the ground. (Depending on where you are, you may need to zoom out and/or turn the camera to see it.)
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step11_Text: Next, click the Station button twice.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step12_Text: Now a small lift hill for a burst of speed. Click the lift chain button first.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step13_Text: Then click the upward slope button five times.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step14_Text: Click the flat piece button twice to level off the hill.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step15_Text: Click the lift chain button to turn the chain off.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step16_Text: Click the downward slope button five times.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step17_Text: Click the flat piece button twice to level off the slope.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step18_Text: Time to split the track in two, with the highlighted 'Toggle split track' button. Click it once to start building the left-hand branch.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step19_Text:
This time we'll build only a short split before joining the track again, but in your own designs each branch can be as wild and inventive as you like.

First, click the left 'Tight Curve' button twice.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step1_Text:
RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Wild! adds these new coasters:

- Coasterball
- Dizzy Dropper
- Drifting Coaster
- Extended Coaster
- Robotic Coaster
- Rotating Tower Coaster
- Spinning Steel
- Splitting Coaster
- Towering Coaster

Most are built with the same coaster tools you know from earlier versions of RCT3. The Splitting Coaster and Robotic Coaster add new parts, which this tutorial covers.

Click Continue to begin.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step20_Text: Next, click the right 'Tight curve' button three times.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step21_Text: Again, click the left 'Tight curve' button twice.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step22_Text: Now build the right-hand branch. Click the 'Toggle split track' button twice to switch to it.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step23_Text: We'll build this branch as a mirror of the left one. First, click the right 'Tight curve' button twice.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step24_Text: Then click the left 'Tight curve' button three times.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step25_Text: Last, click the right 'Tight curve' button twice.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step26_Text: Now merge the two branches back into one. Click the 'Toggle split track' button.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step27_Text: All that's left is joining the track to the station. Click the right 'Medium curve' button three times,
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step29_Text: Let Autocomplete finish the track. Click the Autocomplete button. (It may pause before starting, depending on how fast your PC is.)
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step2_Text:
There's a ready-built Robotic Coaster in this park. Its car carries a robot arm with the seats on the end, and you can set how each part of the arm turns at any point on the track.

Click the coaster to open its panel for the next step.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step30_Text: Wait while the game works out how to finish the track. The autocomplete button flashes when it's done; then click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step31_Text: Click the Autocomplete button to accept its answer.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step32_Text: The game now asks for the coaster's entrance and exit. We only want to test this coaster, so skip that with the close button at the bottom left of the screen.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step33_Text: Click the red flag button, then the amber button, to put the coaster into test mode.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step34_Text:
Well done - you've finished this tutorial! All the buttons for CoasterCam are on if you want to ride the Robotic Coaster and/or the Splitting Coaster.

When building Splitting Coasters, remember each side of the station needs both an entrance and an exit.

Click Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step4_Text: Click the highlighted Robot Arm Angle button near the bottom left of the screen.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step5_Text:
Now you can set how the robot arm turns:

First, click the track piece just after the station to select it.

Then tick the Enable box. A preview of the arm appears on that piece.

The four number spinners set the turn at different joints of the arm: the top one swivels the seats, and the bottom one swivels the arm where it meets the car, for example. Click the up/down arrows, or hold the mouse on a number and drag up or down, to change them.

Once the first piece is set, do the same for other pieces (click a piece and use the robot arm window again) to make the arm move as it travels along the track.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step6_Text:
The buttons down the right of the window help set up the arm positions; hover over each to see what it does.

Close the building window with the close button at the bottom left of the screen to end this part and move on to the Splitting Coaster.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step7_Text: To start building a Splitting Coaster, click the Rides button.
TutorialText_WildCoasters_Step9_Text: Find the Splitting Coaster in the list and click it.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step10_Text: Click the Sold Items button to start choosing what your stall sells.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step11_Text:
Use the '<Select stall type>' drop-down list to pick which stall your custom stall copies. It then works just like any other stall in the game, and you can change what it sells whenever you like.

Close the stall window with the close button at the bottom right of the screen when you want the next step.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step12_Text:
The RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Soaked! expansion let coasters and paths tunnel underground. Wild! keeps that, covered later in this tutorial, and improves tunnels further.

First, you can tunnel into the side of any hill; it no longer needs upright sides.

Second, anything can now be built underground, not only coasters and paths.

Third, the "Terrain Block" scenery items (in the Terrain Surfaces part of the Scenery menu) dig tunnels of your own. That helps when putting scenery underground, as most scenery doesn't dig out the ground itself. Place a terrain block fully underground (hold Shift and drag it down) and a hole appears. Click the hole with the delete tool to fill it in.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step13_Text: That covers what's new in RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Wild! The rest of this tutorial covers features from the RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Soaked! expansion, such as waterfalls, tunnels and loudspeakers. If you own Soaked! and know them already, leave with the Quit button. Otherwise click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step14_Text: Click the highlighted Terrain Tools button to start making your first waterfall.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step16_Text:
To make a waterfall, click the two bodies of water you want to join. Try it with the ones in this park.

Click Continue once you've made a waterfall this way.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step17_Text: With the waterfall tool still picked, right click a waterfall to delete it. Try it, then click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step18_Text:
Players of RollerCoaster Tycoon® 1 and 2 may remember building coasters and paths through cliff faces to make tunnels. Now RCT3 can do it too.

Click the highlighted Rides button to try it.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step1_Text:
This tutorial covers some more new features of RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Wild!, plus some from the last expansion, RollerCoaster Tycoon® 3: Soaked!

Click Continue to begin.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step20_Text: Pick the LIM Launched Coaster from the list. (This coaster needs no lift hills, as it is launched by motors.)
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step21_Text:
The coaster building and testing tools are on. Place the first piece on open ground as usual and build a station as normal. For a tunnel, just build the coaster into a cliff face. The ground turns see-through while you build underground so you can see your work. Tunnel mouths can only be on upright cliff faces.

Click Continue when you've finished trying out tunnels.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step22_Text:
Before we go on, a few more tips on tunnels:

The ride's Vehicles window sets whether underground track pieces have lights, and their color.

Paths can be built underground too.

Click Continue for the next step.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step23_Text:
Several new items go on path edges:

Jumping fountains - they shoot little jets of water to each other in different patterns.

Loudspeakers - they play music anywhere, and also come as scenery for tiles without path.

Passport machines - a guest who visits enough of them gets a free souvenir.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step24_Text: The Ctrl key now helps you place scenery at a set height. Click the highlighted Scenery button to try it.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step26_Text:
Pick any scenery item and place a few on the ground. Place some at different heights by holding Shift and moving the mouse up and down before placing.

Now try holding Ctrl, which does two things. Normally it places the next item at the height of the last one. And if you press Ctrl with the mouse pointer over a scenery item, then next time you hold Ctrl the new piece goes at the height of that 'picked' one.

Click Continue to go on.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step27_Text:
Last, a quick look at a water transport ride. Unlike normal transport rides, it sits on water and needs no track except its stations.

Click the highlighted Rides menu to start building one.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step29_Text: Click 'Paddle Steamer' or 'Air Boat' in the list.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step2_Text: Wild! lets you place billboards to make your park feel more real, and they bring in a little extra money. With an internet connection, the adverts update themselves now and then. You can also make billboards with your own pictures. Click the highlighted Scenery button to start placing one.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step30_Text:
Place the first station piece in the water and add several more - for this ride, stations at least three pieces long work best.

Click Continue once the station is built.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step31_Text: Now place a second station somewhere else. Click the highlighted button left of the track building window; it lets you put the next station piece in a new spot. Try it, and click Continue when you want to go on.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step32_Text: Well done - you've finished this tutorial! Press Quit to go back to the main menu.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step4_Text:
This window lists every advert on offer, with the Custom Image option at the top. Billboards are placed like any scenery: click a picture to pick an advert, pick a billboard type and place it on the ground. Without an internet connection there are no adverts to place.

When you want to go on, click Custom Image to learn how to put your own pictures in the park.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step5_Text:
This window lists what's in your My Pictures folder. Click a picture to make a billboard from it; billboard types appear on the right. Pick one and place it on the ground. (Press Z to turn the billboard before placing it.)

The 'Queue Image' button puts several pictures on one billboard, which shows them one after another.

Place a few custom pictures, then close the billboard list when you want to go on.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step6_Text:
Also new in Wild! is the custom stall, a flexible stall that can act like any other stall in the game. You could, say, make it sell what a balloon stall sells and later switch it to burgers. Custom stalls can also carry billboards.

Click the Shops & Facilities button to start placing one.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step8_Text: Find 'Custom stall' in the list and click it.
TutorialText_WildExtras_Step9_Text: Place the stall on the ground wherever you like.
